publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We propose a unified neural network architecture and learning algorithm that can be applied to various natural language processing tasks including: part-of-speech tagging, chunking, named entity recognition, and semantic role labeling.

span.label: neural sequence labelling across NLP benchmark tasks
span.quote: All the NLP tasks above can be seen as tasks assigning labels to words.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We implemented a standalone version of our architecture, written in the C language.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE FIELD'S GOAL IS POSED AS A QUESTION AND THEN REPORTED TO HAVE NO AGREED FORM: will a program ever convert English text into a data structure that UNAMBIGUOUSLY AND COMPLETELY DESCRIBES THE MEANING - and AMONG NUMEROUS PROBLEMS, NO CONSENSUS HAS EMERGED ABOUT THE FORM OF SUCH A DATA STRUCTURE. The obstacle named first is not difficulty but the absence of agreement on what the answer would look like
span.quote: Will a computer program ever be able to convert a piece of English text into a data structure that unambiguously and completely describes the meaning of the natural language text? Among numerous problems, no consensus has emerged about the form of such a data structure.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE FIELD'S TASKS ARE NAMED AS REDUCED OBJECTIVES ADOPTED BECAUSE THE REAL QUESTION IS UNRESOLVED: UNTIL SUCH FUNDAMENTAL PROBLEMS ARE RESOLVED, computer scientists MUST SETTLE FOR REDUCED OBJECTIVES - extracting SIMPLER REPRESENTATIONS describing RESTRICTED ASPECTS of the textual information. **What the field measures itself on is described as a substitute, in the paper's second sentence**
span.quote: Until such fundamental Artificial Intelligence problems are resolved, computer scientists must settle for reduced objectives: extracting simpler representations describing restricted aspects of the textual information.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SAME REPRESENTATIONS ARE GIVEN TWO DIFFERENT WARRANTS, AND ONE OF THEM IS A BELIEF: they are OFTEN MOTIVATED BY SPECIFIC APPLICATIONS, for instance bag-of-words for information retrieval - and they CAN ALSO BE MOTIVATED BY OUR BELIEF THAT THEY CAPTURE SOMETHING MORE GENERAL about natural language. An instrumental justification and an epistemic one, offered for the same objects
span.quote: These simpler representations are often motivated by specific applications, for instance, bag-of-words variants for information retrieval. These representations can also be motivated by our belief that they capture something more general about natural language.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE ANNOTATIONS EXIST IN ORDER TO MAKE SYSTEMS COMPARABLE, AND THE BENCHMARKS ARE CREDITED WITH DRIVING THE RESEARCH: text corpora HAVE BEEN MANUALLY ANNOTATED with such data structures IN ORDER TO COMPARE THE PERFORMANCE of various systems, and THE AVAILABILITY OF STANDARD BENCHMARKS HAS STIMULATED RESEARCH. The ground truth's purpose is comparison, and the comparison is what made the field move
span.quote: Text corpora have been manually annotated with such data structures in order to compare the performance of various systems. The availability of standard benchmarks has stimulated research in Natural Language Processing (NLP)

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE METHOD IS DEFINED BY WHAT IT REFUSES TO USE, AND THE COST IS STATED IN THE SAME SENTENCE: the versatility is achieved BY TRYING TO AVOID TASK-SPECIFIC ENGINEERING AND THEREFORE DISREGARDING A LOT OF PRIOR KNOWLEDGE - instead of exploiting MAN-MADE INPUT FEATURES carefully optimized for each task. What is given up is named as the price of what is gained
span.quote: This versatility is achieved by trying to avoid task-specific engineering and therefore disregarding a lot of prior knowledge. Instead of exploiting man-made input features carefully optimized for each task, our system learns internal representations on the basis of vast amounts of mostly unlabeled training data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE GROUND TRUTH ITSELF COMES IN TWO VOCABULARIES, AND THE FIX IS TO PICK ONE: the ground truth for three of the tasks IS PROVIDED USING TWO DIFFERENT TAGGING SCHEMES, and IN ORDER TO ELIMINATE THIS ADDITIONAL SOURCE OF VARIATIONS the authors DECIDED TO USE THE MOST EXPRESSIVE scheme FOR ALL TASKS. **Two naming systems for the same annotations, normalised by choosing the more expressive - not the more common**
span.quote: The ground truth for the NER, CHUNK, and SRL tasks is provided using two different tagging schemes. In order to eliminate this additional source of variations, we have decided to use the most expressive IOBES tagging scheme for all tasks.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE CHOICE OF HYPER-PARAMETERS IS CONCEDED TO BE ONE OF MANY EQUALLY GOOD ONES, WITH THE UNEXPLORED SPACE NAMED: although they ended up with A PARTICULAR CHOICE, MANY OTHER CHOICES ARE ALMOST EQUALLY AS GOOD - ALTHOUGH PERHAPS THERE ARE OTHERS THAT ARE BETTER, AS WE COULD NOT DO A FULL GRID SEARCH. The reported configuration is presented as a sample rather than an optimum
span.quote: However, we should say we believe that although we ended up with a particular choice of parameters, many other choices are almost equally as good, although perhaps there are others that are better as we could not do a full grid search.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SCALE OF THE EXPERIMENT IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE HARDWARE RATHER THAN TO THE SCIENCE, WRYLY: very long training times MAKE SUCH STRATEGIES NECESSARY FOR THE FORESEEABLE FUTURE - and IF WE HAD BEEN GIVEN COMPUTERS TEN TIMES FASTER, WE PROBABLY WOULD HAVE FOUND USES FOR DATASETS TEN TIMES BIGGER. The design is described as a function of the machines available
span.quote: Very long training times make such strategies necessary for the foreseeable future: if we had been given computers ten times faster, we probably would have found uses for datasets ten times bigger.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: TWO NEGATIVE RESULTS FROM OTHER GROUPS ARE CITED SIDE BY SIDE: one group obtained results SOMEWHAT BELOW THE STATE-OF-THE-ART using joint decoding for two tasks, and another DESCRIBED A NEGATIVE RESULT AT THE SAME JOINT TASK. Failures are gathered as evidence about a practice rather than about the groups that attempted it
span.quote: On the other hand, Sutton and McCallum (2005a) obtain results somewhat below the state-of-the-art using joint decoding for SRL and syntactic parsing. Musillo and Merlo (2006) also describe a negative result at the same joint task.

span.label: avoiding task-specific features meant forgoing a large body of linguistic knowledge
span.quote: Our desire to avoid task-specific engineered features led us to ignore a large body of linguistic knowledge.

span.label: The system is only 'almost' from scratch: words are lowercased and capitalization encoded, and learning from letter sequences was left out of scope.
span.quote: Ideally, an even more raw input would be to learn from letter sequences rather than words, however we felt that this was beyond the scope of this work.

span.label: Week-long training times made a proper hyperparameter search infeasible.
span.quote: Since training times for such large scale systems are counted in weeks, it is not feasible to try many combinations of hyperparameters.

span.label: Multi-task learning gave no or only marginal gains over separately trained per-task architectures.
span.quote: While we find worth mentioning that MTL can produce a single unified architecture that performs well for all these tasks, no (or only marginal) improvements were obtained with this approach compared to training separate architectures per task (which still use semisupervised learning, which is somehow the most important MTL task).

span.label: The language model structure is probably too restrictive to capture hierarchical syntax; only the word embeddings are exploited downstream.
span.quote: On the other hand, the structure of our language models is probably too restrictive for such goals, and our current approach only exploits the word embeddings discovered during training.

span.label: The benchmark scores are treated as indirect measurements of something the paper does not measure directly, and the claim about it is a posit.
span.quote: In fact we view the benchmarks as indirect measurements of the relevance of the internal representations discovered by the learning procedure, and we posit that these intermediate representations are more general than any of the benchmarks

span.label: The paper names the failure mode its own design is exposed to.
span.quote: On the other hand, there is a great temptation to optimize the performance of a system for a specific benchmark

span.label: The pre-processing the architecture does keep is named, with a presumably attached to removing it.
span.quote: We did some pre-processing, namely lowercasing and encoding capitalization as another feature. With enough (unlabeled) training data, presumably we could learn a model without this processing

span.label: Task-specific engineering is added back in a later section, so the headline architecture and the best numbers are not the same system.
span.quote: Section 6 then evaluates how much further improvement can be achieved by incorporating standard NLP task-specific engineering into our systems
